newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Low quantities firm prices at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Low quantities firm prices at Colombo auction.

text.p: Rubber prices were firm at the Colombo auction where quantities remained low due to rain in growing areas, brokers and buyers said.
"To collect a container-load of rubber these days one needs to go to the auction for about one month," said Lanil Waniganayake of export firm Almar Trading Co.
"Sentiment is very firm. Shippers are under pressure to buy whatever is available," he said.
On offer was 144 tonnes, about half the quantity that is usually sold over the Colombo auction.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, fetched 88 rupees ($1.50) per kg compared to 87.50 last week. Number one rose to 87 rupees from 86 last week, while RSS 1 fetched 63.65 rupees after going unquoted the week before, according to brokerage John Keells.
Brokers said demand for sole crepe was also high, which firms sentiment in the Colombo market. Sri Lanka is the world's biggest sole crepe manufacturer.

But rain in growing areas was likely to keep quantities depressed in coming weeks, they said. Rain, which immediately hampers rubber tapping, in the long-term also reduces latex quality. ($1=58.34) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319rub/lk
